IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r5.claim: The source identifies the الإنسان in the cited Nahl, Maryam, and Yā Sīn verses as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r5.anchor: والحادي والعشرون : أبي بن خلف . [ ومنه ] قوله تعالى في النحل : ﴿ خلق الإنسان من نطفة ﴾

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p278#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p278#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p278#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed when Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought the Prophet a decayed bone and challenged whether God could revive it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p278#2/r1.anchor: نزلت الآية في أبي بن خلف الجمحي حين جاء بعظم رميم إلى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقال: يا محمد

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p278#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p278#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p278#2/r2.claim: The author links this verse to the parallel passage in Yasin, which he says was revealed about the same incident.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p278#2/r2.anchor: نظير هذه الآية قوله تعالى في سورة يس: {أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين}

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Verses 1–9 warn Quraysh that punishment approaches, reject reliance on partners, affirm accountability for purposeful creation, and direct people toward God's straight path.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The disbelievers of the Quraysh are warned that they should know that God’s torment is just about to arrive.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Here human being refers to the idolaters and disbelievers under discussion, who are left unnamed to express the author's aversion to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: They are not named to express aversion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The human, made from an impure drop, becomes God's inveterate enemy and denies resurrection; the source links this hostility to the coming challenge over God's associates.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: such is the audacity of a human being created from an impure drop of water that he has become an inveterate foe of God

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r9.claim: After the external proof from cosmic creation, God gives an argument from the human being’s own creation from a sperm drop; humans should obey rather than quarrel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r9.anchor: ولما ذكر ما دل على وحدانيته من خلق العالم العلوي والأرض،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r10.claim: “Contentious” is an intensive noun for one who disputes or a disputant, and “manifest” means either plainly contentious or one who makes contention plain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r10.anchor: والخصيم من صفات المبالغة من خصم بمعنى اختصم، أو بمعنى مخاصم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r11.claim: The context most naturally condemns humans for disputing God’s messengers with false arguments; elsewhere scripture usually presents the human being in a blameworthy setting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن سياق هذين الوصفين سياق ذم لما تقدم من قوله: سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r1.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r1.claim: Some identify the human being in the verse as Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالإنسان هنا أبي بن خلف الجمحي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r2.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r2.claim: Others take the two descriptions as praise: God enabled a human to dispute and distinguish truth from falsehood, and elevated him from sperm to articulate speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: سياق الوصفين سياق المدح، لأنه تعالى قواه على منازعة الخصوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r3.claim: “Then” marks suddenness after the human’s formation, while the developmental stages between sperm and speech are left unstated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r3.anchor: وإذ هنا للمفاجأة، وبعد خلقه من النطفة لم تقع المفاجأة بالمخاطبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi argues at length that humans are the noblest bodies after the celestial spheres and stars; Abu Hayyan rejects the claim that those spheres outrank humans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p505#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: اعلم أن أشرف الأجسام بعد الأفلاك والكواكب

TABATABAI:16:1-21#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:1-21#4/r8.speaker: الإمام
TABATABAI:16:1-21#4/r8.claim: The commentary says the human is created from a lowly drop yet becomes a clear, eloquent disputant.
TABATABAI:16:1-21#4/r8.anchor: في قوله تعالى { فإذا هو خصيم مبين } قال عليه السلام خلقه من قطرة من ماء مهين فيكون خصيما متكلما بليغا.

STUDYQURAN:16:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r1.claim: Humanity’s creation from a drop of fluid evokes essential weakness and helplessness.
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r1.anchor: That human beings were created from a drop of fluid (cf. 18:37; 22:5; 23:12–14; 35:11; 40:67; 53:45–46; 75:37; 76:2; 80:19) evokes their essential weakness (IK)

STUDYQURAN:16:4/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r2.speaker: IK, Z
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r2.claim: People become manifest adversaries of their Lord by denying His power and the blessings He has given them.
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r2.anchor: Human beings are a manifest adversary of the Lord (IK, Z) insofar as they deny His Power and the blessings He has bestowed upon them

STUDYQURAN:16:4/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r3.claim: Their enmity includes refusing to believe God can resurrect the dead.
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r3.anchor: and refuse to believe in His ability to resurrect the dead (R), although they were created to be servants

STUDYQURAN:16:4/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r4.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r4.claim: Although created to serve God, humans oppose Him.
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r4.anchor: although they were created to be servants (51:56), not opponents (IK). This verse was reportedly revealed

STUDYQURAN:16:4/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r5.speaker: W
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r5.claim: The verse was reportedly revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who doubted that God could resurrect the dead.
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r5.anchor: This verse was reportedly revealed in reference to Ubayy ibn Khalaf, a Makkan who expressed skepticism about God’s ability to resurrect the dead (W).

STUDYQURAN:16:4/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r6.claim: The verse’s wording about creation from a drop is echoed in 36:77.
STUDYQURAN:16:4/r6.anchor: See also commentary on 36:77: Has not man seen that We created him from a drop and, behold, he is a manifest adversary.

TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r1.claim: God develops a human from a lowly drop through successive stages in three darknesses, breathes in the spirit, and feeds and grows him to maturity; the human then denies the creator and disputes with Him.
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r1.anchor: ونفخ فيه الروح، فغذاه ورزقه القوت ونماه

TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r2.claim: The human forgets the one who formed him and argues against God, even asking who can revive decayed bones, as in 36:78.

TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r3.claim: Mubīn means that a person makes his dispute clear through articulate speech and argument with his tongue.
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r3.anchor: ويعني بالمبين: أنه يبين عن خصومته بمنطقه ويجادل بلسانه

TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r4.claim: Al-insān is grammatically singular here but denotes humanity as a whole.
TAB-FULL:v14p165#2/r4.anchor: وعنى بالإنسان: جميع الناس، أخرج بلفظ الواحد وهو في معنى الجميع

TABATABAI:16:2-4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r3.claim: Creation manifests divinity, while created things serving as blessings for people imply an integrated order and one governor; God alone is Lord of humanity and all things.
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r3.anchor: فإن الخلق والإيجاد آية الألوهية وكون الخلق بعضها نعمة بالنسبة إلى بعض آية الربوبية

TABATABAI:16:2-4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r4.claim: The human created from a drop refers to reproduction within the human species, not the exceptional creations of Adam and Jesus.
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r4.anchor: المراد به الخلق الجاري في النوع الإنساني وهو جعل نسله من النطفة فلا يشمل آدم وعيسى عليهما السلام

TABATABAI:16:2-4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r5.claim: خصيم is an adjective describing one prone to disputation and argument.
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r5.anchor: والخصيم صفة مشبهة من الخصومة وهي الجدال

TABATABAI:16:2-4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r6.claim: Although the verse could express the blessing of transforming a contemptible drop into an articulate human, its rebuking context favors condemnation of human audacity in disputing with God.
TABATABAI:16:2-4/r6.anchor: لكن كثرة الآيات التي توبخ الإنسان وتقرعه على وقاحته في خصامه في ربه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#4/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#4/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq says this verse compresses the account of human development, which the Qur’an describes in detail elsewhere.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#4/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: اختصر هاهنا، وذكر تقلب أحوال الإنسان في غير مكان من القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the words as “I created.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد إني خلقت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r2.claim: The commentators say this verse and 36:77 were revealed concerning Ubayy ibn Khalaf and his denial of resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون: نزلت هذه الآية والتي في آخر سورة يس: {أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة} [يس: 77] في قصة أبي بن خلف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r3.claim: Khaṣīm means disputant, as in 4:105; the lexicographers analyze faʿīl as carrying the sense of an active participant and cite nasīb, ʿashīr, akīl, and sharīb.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r3.anchor: الخصيم بمعنى المخاصم، ذكرنا ذلك عند قوله: {ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما} [النساء: 105]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r4.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r4.claim: Alternatively, khaṣīm may be an active form from khaṣama/yakhṣimu, meaning “to dispute”; Hamza’s reading yakhṣimūn at 36:49 illustrates this formation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون خصيم فاعلا من خصم يخصم بمعنى اختصم، وبه قرأ حمزة (¬1) قوله: {تأخذهم وهم يخصمون} (¬2) [يس: 49]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r5.claim: Mubīn means apparent, so the person is clearly contentious; it can also mean that he articulates his contention, though falsely.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {مبين} أي ظاهر، ومعناه: ظاهر الخصومة، ويجوز أن يكون مبين؛ أي يبين عن نفسه الخصومة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r6.claim: The semanticists offer two senses: God demonstrates His power by bringing a fully formed disputant from a drop, or exposes the grave ingratitude of disputing His divinity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p11#5/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل المعاني لهذه الآية معنيين؛ أحدهما: أنه عرفنا قدرته في إخراجه من النطفة ما هذه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:1-4/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:1-4/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:1-4/r9.claim: The human created from a drop of fluid is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:1-4/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:1-4/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:1-4/r10.claim: Ubayy became an outspoken disputant by arguing with the Prophet over denial of resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:1-4/r10.anchor: وذلك أنه خاصم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في إنكاره البعث

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p50/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p50/r5.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p50/r5.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the disputatious human as the polytheist.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p50/r5.anchor: وتفسير الحسن أنه المشرك. قال وهو كقوله:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p50/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p50/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p50/r6.claim: He compares this to the passage where a human disputes resurrection after forgetting his creation from a drop.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p50/r6.anchor: أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين

ELMALILI:16:4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:16:4/r1.claim: A drop of semen is a lowly, weak fluid, so creating a human from it demonstrates immense divine power.
ELMALILI:16:4/r1.anchor: bir nutfe, bir meni katresi ne hakir bir mâyi‘, ne âciz bir şeydir? Ve ondan bir insan yaratmak ne büyük kudrettir.

ELMALILI:16:4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:16:4/r2.claim: By God’s power and the spirit He breathed into him, a human gains sensation, will, speech, eloquence, and strength.
ELMALILI:16:4/r2.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın kudretiyle, Allah’ın ona nefhettiği rûh ile hiss ü irade, nutk u beyan sâhibi kavî bir insan kılığına girer

ELMALILI:16:4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:16:4/r3.claim: The human fashioned from a drop quickly becomes an articulate disputant, able to argue in self-defense.
ELMALILI:16:4/r3.anchor: mübîn bir muhâsım kesilir kendini müdafaa yolunda natûk bir münazaracı, mücadeleci hâline gelir

ELMALILI:16:4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:16:4/r4.claim: Forgetting his origin, a person may openly oppose his Creator, associate partners with Him, and argue through logic and philosophy.
ELMALILI:16:4/r4.anchor: veya mâhiyetini unutur da Hâlıkına karşı bile açık bir muhâsım olur. O’na karşı şirk koşmaya, mantık ve felsefeden bahsetmeye kalkışır.

ELMALILI:16:4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:16:4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:16:4/r5.claim: Injustice occurs only among humans in the created world, which is why the warning is directed to them.
ELMALILI:16:4/r5.anchor: Ve binâen‘aleyh bütün bu âlemde haksızlık yalnız insanlarda bulunur. Ve onun içindir ki inzar emri de insanlara teveccüh eder.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r1.claim: After affirming God's transcendence from partners and His sole divinity, the passage through verse 18 adduces signs of His existence, unity, and creative power, recalls blessings, and urges gratitude.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r1.anchor: 18. âyete kadar olan bölümde de bu gerçeği kanıtlamak üzere O’nun varlığının, birliğinin ve yaratıcı kudretinin bazı delilleri gösterilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r2.claim: The creation of the heavens and earth as the great world, and the human as the small world, together with nature fitted to benefit people, attest to God's existence and wise creative power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r2.anchor: Tasavvuf ve felsefe kültüründe “büyük âlem” denilen yer ve göklerle “küçük âlem” denilen insanın yaratılması ve yaratılış keyfiyeti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r4.claim: Human beings alone among earthly creatures can oppose God; being made from a drop yet given agency and freedom to defy their creator is a sign of divine power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r4.anchor: Yeryüzünde insandan başka hiçbir varlık Allah’a karşı gelme gücüne ve özgürlüğüne sahip değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r5.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r5.claim: Razi describes the human's rise from an ordinary thing to a lofty and honored rank as evidence of the Creator's power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:3/r5.anchor: alelâde bir nesne iken böylesine yüksek ve şerefli bir düzeye ulaşması

BURHAN:v1p84/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p84/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p84/r1.claim: The opening of al-Nahl moves from the heavens to human creation, livestock, and plants; the plant passage ends with reflection because diverse plant kinds point to a powerful, freely acting God.
BURHAN:v1p84/r1.anchor: في أوائل النحل وذلك أنه سبحانه بدأ فيها بذكر الأفلاك

SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r1.claim: من نطفة depends on خلق, and من marks the beginning of the process.

SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r2.claim: نطفة means a drop of water; the verb نطف describes dripping, as in water dripping from someone's head.
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r2.anchor: والنطفة: القطرة من الماء، نطف رأسه ماء، أي: قطر.

SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r3.claim: نطفة can also mean clear water, euphemistically refer to male fluid, or designate a pearl; صبي منطف has a pearl in his ear.
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r3.anchor: وقيل: هي الماء الصافي ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل، ويكنى بها عن اللؤلؤة، ومنه صبي منطف: إذا كان في أذنه لؤلؤة،

SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r4.claim: ليلة نطوف is a night with rain; الناطف is a liquid that flows, from نطف ينطف, 'to flow.'
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r4.anchor: ويقال: ليلة نطوف: إذا جاء فيها مطر. والناطف: ما سال من المائعات، نطف ينطف، أي: سال فهو ناطف.

SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r5.claim: The clause فإذا هو خصيم follows the preceding clause; the author addresses its apparent suddenness despite the many stages between conception and adulthood.
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r5.anchor: عطف هذه الجملة على ما قبلها. فإن قيل: الفاء تدل على التعقيب، ولا سيما وقد وجد معها " إذا "

SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r6.claim: One explanation uses an eventual state for the thing's present name, as in 'I press wine' for grapes; another highlights how quickly people forget their origin.
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r6.anchor: أنه من باب التعبير عن حال الشيء بما يؤول إليه، كقوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r7.claim: A further explanation assumes omitted stages between the drop and the adult disputant.

SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r8.claim: The author says خلق covers bringing the human into being and nurturing him until he reaches the two described qualities.
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r8.anchor: والذي يظهر أن قوله " خلق " عبارة عن إيجاده وتربيته إلى أن يبلغ حد هاتين الصفتين.

SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r9.claim: خصيم is an intensive فعيل from خصم meaning to dispute; it can alternatively mean مخاصم, like خليط and جليس.
SAMIN-DURR:16:4/r9.anchor: و " خصيم " فعيل، مثال مبالغة من خصم بمعنى اختصم، ويجوز أن يكون مخاصم كالخليط والجليس.

ZAJJAJ:v3p190/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p190/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p190/r5.claim: This verse abbreviates the account of human development; the Qur'an recounts the changing stages of human life elsewhere.
ZAJJAJ:v3p190/r5.anchor: اختصر ههنا، وذكر تقلب أحوال الإنسان في غير مكان

ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r1.claim: One Zamakhshari reading stresses God's creative power: a once-inert sperm-drop becomes articulate and able to argue clearly and courageously.
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r1.anchor: Zamakhshari, "one interpretation is that after having been a (mere] drop of sperm

ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r2.claim: His other reading is that a human may contend against his Sustainer and refuse to acknowledge the Creator.
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r2.anchor: According to Zamakhshari and Razi, the above phrase is liable to two interpretations

ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r3.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r3.claim: Razi unequivocally supports the first reading because the passage emphasizes evidence for a wise Creator, not human insolence or ingratitude.
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r3.anchor: Razi, on his part, gives his. unqualified. support to the first of these two interpretations

ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r4.claim: Asad regards both readings as complementary: rationality can raise humans to great achievements or lead them astray, as 36:77-78 illustrates.
ASAD-NOTES:16:4#n5/r4.anchor: I am of the opinion that the above two interpretations are not mutually exclusive but, rather, complementary

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r4.claim: Al-Nahl first speaks of humanity’s creation and then livestock created for people; al-Zumar first mentions Adam and Eve, then their descendants and provisions.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1065/r4.anchor: هذا خلقنا نحن وليس آدم ثم ذكر بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r1.claim: Al-insān here means the human species, not its first individual.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r1.anchor: أي هذا النوع غير الفرد الأول منه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r2.claim: Nuṭfa originally means clear water and is used for man’s semen; humanity is created from lifeless, flowing substance that retains no shape or position.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r2.anchor: أصلها الماء الصافي ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل أي أوجده من جماد لا حس له ولا حراك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r3.claim: Khaṣīm means an eloquent, forceful disputant who argues for himself and confronts opponents; its form is intensive.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r3.anchor: منطيق مجادل عن نفسه مكافح للخصوم وهو صيغة مبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r4.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r4.claim: Al-Wāḥidī glosses khaṣīm as mukhāṣim, noting that faʿīl can mean mufāʿil, as in words for relative and companion.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r4.anchor: وقال الواحدي : بمعنى مخاصم وفعيل بمعنى مفاعل معروف عندهم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r5.claim: Mubīn means that the human displays an argument taught to him.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r6.claim: Another reading makes the human a disputant against his Creator, denying divine power and asking who revives decayed bones; Al-Ālūsī prefers ability to reason as better suited to the blessing context.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : المعنى أوجده من ذلك فإذا هو خصيم لخالقه سبحانه منكر لعظيم قدرته

ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r7.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r7.claim: The Imam says the opening points to proof from the body, while the ending points to proof from the human soul and its development.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r7.anchor: اعلم أن الإنسان مركب من نفس وبدن وصدر الآية إشارة إلى الاستدلال ببدنه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r8.claim: If the drop’s components are alike, nature would produce a sphere, not a human body; if unlike, natural governance would make its simple elements spherical, not the observed body, requiring a wise choosing agent.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p96#2/r8.anchor: فإن كان الأول لم يجز أن يكون المقتضي لتولد هذا البدن منها هو الطبيعة الحاصلة في جوهرها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r1.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r1.claim: The passage rejects stellar influence on human formation: celestial effects are uniform, and their efficacy has been disproved elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r1.anchor: لأن تأثيراتها متشابهة على أنه قد بين بطلان كونها مؤثرة بغير ذلك في موضعه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r2.claim: The Imam contrasts a chick that quickly distinguishes foes and food with a human infant who cannot, then becomes highly discerning.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r2.anchor: فإن فرخ الدجاجة حين خروجه من قشر البيضة يميز بين العدو والصديق فيهرب من الهرة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r3.claim: A human’s transformation from infant dullness to mature knowledge of God, creation, and debate requires a wise God to perfect the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r3.anchor: فانتقال نفسه من تلك البلادة المفرطة إلى هذه الكياسة المفرطة لا بد وأن يكون بتدبير إله مختار حكيم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r4.claim: Some consider the disputatiousness reading apt in a list of unbelievers’ offenses because it portrays their audacity and persistence in disbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r4.anchor: والثاني قيل : أنسب بمقام تعداد هنات الكفرة فإنه قد اشتمل من بيان جراءة من كفر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r5.claim: Some cite the parallel in Yā Sīn about who can revive decayed bones as support for the audacity reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r5.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنه يؤيد هذا الوجه قوله تعالى في سورة يس بعد ما ذكر مثله

ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the Yā Sīn parallel does not settle this verse: that sūra’s context centers on resurrection denial, unlike this passage.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r6.anchor: وتعقب بأنه ليس بشيء لأنه مدار ما قبلها في تلك السورة على ذكر الحشر والنشر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r7.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r7.claim: Al-Kashf finds both readings suitable, but the audacity reading fits ‘exalted above their associations’ better and incorporates the first reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r7.anchor: وفي الكشف المعنيان ملائمان للمقام إلا أن في الثاني زيادة ملائمة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r8.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r8.claim: Al-Wāḥidī reports that Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought a decayed bone to the Prophet and asked if God would revive it; the account says a parallel passage was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r8.anchor: وروي الواحدي أن أبي بن خلف أتى النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that the well-known account assigns revelation for Ubayy’s challenge to the ending of Yā Sīn, not this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r9.anchor: والمشهور أن تلك هي النازلة في تلك القصة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r10.claim: The sudden ‘then’ skips no necessary stage: it presents eventual rational maturity as the culmination after the drop.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p97/r10.anchor: أنه بيان لأطواره إلى كمال عقله فالتعقيب باعتبار آخرها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r2.claim: Humans are created from a drop yet become manifest disputants, arguing falsely.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r2.anchor: {خلق الإنسان من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم} جدل بالباطل، {مبين}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r3.claim: The verse was said to be revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who denied resurrection and brought a decayed bone to challenge its revival; the same occasion is linked to 36:77.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r3.anchor: نزلت في أبي بن خلف الجمحي، وكان ينكر البعث جاء بعظم رميم فقال: أتقول إن الله تعالى يحيي هذا بعدما قد رم؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r4.claim: Baghawī says the sounder view is that the verse is general: it demonstrates God's power and exposes the ugliness of denying His evident blessings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p9/r4.anchor: والصحيح أن الآية عامة، وفيها بيان القدرة وكشف قبيح ما فعلوه، من جحد نعم الله مع ظهورها عليهم (2)

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r1.claim: Humanity was created from a fluid, insentient and motionless substance that cannot retain a position or shape.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r1.anchor: جماد لا حس بها ولا حراك سيالة

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r2.claim: خصيم مبين means an eloquent disputant who makes an argument clear, or one who openly confronts his Creator and asks who can revive decayed bones.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r2.anchor: { مبين } للحجة أو خصيم مكافح لخالقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r3.speaker: أبي بن خلف
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r3.claim: A report says Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought the Prophet a decayed bone, challenged whether God could revive it, and the verse was revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:4-5/r3.anchor: روي أن أبي بن خلف أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم رميم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r1.claim: Human creation is an especially strong proof of divine oneness and deliberate action: the human is the noblest body in the lower world and cannot be nobler than its Lord.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r1.anchor: أي هذا النوع الذي خلقه أدل ما يكون على الوحدانية والفعل بالاختيار

BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r2.claim: Humans surpass other animals through the noble powers of outward and inward senses, appetite and anger, and speech, which grasps universals and works with analogical reasoning.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r3.claim: Adam was created from unqualified water, whereas his descendants were created from specific, ejaculated fluid.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r3.anchor: أي آدم عليه السلام من مطلق الماء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r4.claim: The human made from humble water becomes eloquent and skilled in disputation, displaying speech and understanding despite having had no sensation or voluntary movement before.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r5.claim: The transformation from inert fluid to an articulate disputant proves the creator’s complete power and choice; the one who originated humanity can also restore it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p245/r5.anchor: أفلا يقدر الذي ابتدأ ذلك على إعادته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r1.claim: This resumes the proof of God's unique divinity: after visible cosmic creation, human creation is evidence known to people and especially wondrous in its transformation from a lowly drop to articulate intellect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r1.anchor: وهو استدلال آخر على انفراده تعالى بالإلهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r2.claim: الإنسان is definite for mental reference, a generic term for the known species called human.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r3.claim: The verse invites reflection on human nature and traits, the species' other conditions, its lowly beginning as a noble kind, and its elevated culmination in intellect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر للاعتبار بخلق الإنسان ثلاثة اعتبارات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r4.claim: خصيم is an intensive form meaning one who disputes often.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r5.claim: مبين is a second predicate of هو: the human can articulate intentions and argue truth or falsehood with many kinds of proof, even sophistry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r5.anchor: و { مبين } خبر ثانن عن ضمير { فإذا هو }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r6.claim: The dispute is human advocacy of partners, rejection of divine unity, and denial of those who call to monotheism, as the parallel in Yasin makes explicit.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r7.claim: إذا is a transferred metaphor for an outcome contrary to what reflection predicts: instead of recognizing the Creator and resurrection, humans dispute unity and resurrection as if surprising an observer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p102/r7.anchor: والإتيان بحرف ( إذا ) المفاجأة استعارة تبعية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103/r1.claim: The suddenness marker combines admiration at humanity's rise from the lowliest state to rational eloquence with amazement at its ingratitude in using God's gifts to disobey Him; plain فهو خصيم or فكان خصيما would lose this effect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103/r1.anchor: فإقحام حرف المفاجأة جعل الكلام مفهما أمرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103#2/r1.claim: One parsing coordinates الأنعام with الإنسان; livestock too are created from a drop, making their wondrous formation parallel evidence, while خلقها begins a new sentence of benefaction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103#2/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يعطف { الأنعام } عطف المفرد على المفرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103#2/r4.claim: The first parsing more fully balances reflection on creation followed by an allusion to ingratitude; the second states benefaction directly and implies reflection through emphasis. Neither parsing asserts exclusivity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p103#2/r4.anchor: إلا أن الوجه الأول تمام مقابلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r10.claim: ‘Humankind’ means the species; God names its two extremes to display the vast change between them through divine power.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r10.anchor: وقوله خلق الإنسان من نطفة يريد ب الإنسان الجنس، وأخذ له الغايتين ليظهر له البعد بينهما بقدرة الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r11.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r11.claim: A report says this verse was revealed in response to Ubayy ibn Khalaf’s challenge, ‘Who revives the bones when they are dust?’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r11.anchor: ويروى أن الآية نزلت لقول أبي بن خلف من يحيي العظام وهي رميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r12.speaker: الحسن البصري عن ابن سلام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r12.claim: Ibn Salam transmits from Hasan al-Basri that ‘a clear disputant’ means unbelievers who argue against God and debate His oneness and law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r12.anchor: خصيم يحتمل أن يريد به الكفرة الذين يختصمون في الله ويجادلون في توحيده وشرعه، ذكره ابن سلام عن الحسن البصري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r13.claim: Alternatively, the verse addresses humanity broadly and counts intellect and speech as blessings; in the context of unbelievers’ disputes, it adds a warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p378#2/r13.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد أعم من هذا على أن الآية تعديد نعمة الذهن والبيان على البشر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r1.claim: The commentators say the verse was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who crumbled a decayed bone and challenged Muhammad over resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون أخذ أبي بن خلف عظما رميما فجعل يفته ويقول يامحمد كيف يبعت الله هذا بعدما رم فنزلت فيه هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r2.claim: Khasīm means disputatious; mubīn means manifest or evident in dispute.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r3.claim: Although created from a drop, a person disputes and denies resurrection; the one able to create initially can restore life.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r3.anchor: والمعنى أنه مخلوق من نطفة وهو مع ذلك يخاصم وينكر البعث أفلا يستدل بأولة على آخرة وأن من قدر على إيجادة أولا يقدر على إعادتة ثانية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r4.claim: The verse also recalls God's favor in raising humans from the weakness of a drop to strength sufficient for argument.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p428/r4.anchor: وفية تنبية علي إنعام الله علية حين نقلة من حال ضعف النطفة إلى القوة التي أمكنة معها الخصام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r3.claim: Humanity begins as a weak, lowly drop, yet once grown people dispute with their Lord, deny Him, and fight His messengers; they were created to serve, not oppose, Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r3.anchor: ثم نبه على خلق جنس الإنسان {من نطفة} أي: ضعيفة مهينة، فلما استقل ودرج إذا هو يخاصم ربه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r4.claim: The contrast between human creation and defiance is linked to human creation from water and taking other than God as protectors, and to the human who forgets his origin and disputes resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r4.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {وهو الذي خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا وكان ربك قديرا * ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعهم ولا يضرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r5.speaker: بسر بن جحاش عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r5.claim: A hadith says God addresses Adam’s child: He created him from a drop, gave him form, then he strutted, amassed and withheld wealth, and only at death’s throat offered charity too late.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p556#3/r5.anchor: عن بسر بن جحاش قال: بصق رسول الله في كفه، ثم قال:

JISHUMI:v6p3999/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r3.claim: Khasm is used for one or many and for either gender, like ʿadl; it is best treated as a verbal noun meaning one who has contention, though it can take dual and plural forms and خصام can be either plural or verbal noun.
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r3.anchor: الخصم: معروف، ويستوي فيه الواحد والجماعة، والذكر والأنثى، يقال: رجل خصم ورجال خصم، وامرأة خصم، ونساء خصم

JISHUMI:v6p3999/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r4.claim: Abu Muslim says a khasim is strong in disputing opponents.
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r4.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: الخصيم القوي علي منازعة الخصوم.

JISHUMI:v6p3999/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، والحسن
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan report that the verse was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, who brought the Prophet a decayed bone and challenged whether God could revive it; the cited wording is 36:77.
JISHUMI:v6p3999/r9.anchor: فنزلت الآية فيه: (أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة) عن ابن عباس، والحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r1.claim: خصيم means someone who argues in a dispute.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r2.claim: مبين describes someone who clearly expresses what is within him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r2.anchor: والمبين هو المفصح عما في ضميره

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r3.claim: The contrast displays God's power in bringing a human from a lowly drop to eloquence and capability.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r3.anchor: إخراجه من النطفة المهينة إلى أن صار بهذه الحال في البيان والمكنة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r4.claim: The description should make people recognize God's favor in bringing them from a lowly drop to their present state.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r4.anchor: ليعرفه نعم الله تعالى عليه في إخراجه إلى هذه الحال بعدما خلقه من نطفة مهينة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r5.claim: The description exposes the gross ingratitude of wasting God's favor by disputing in disbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r5.anchor: فاحش ما ارتكب من تضييع النعمة بالخصومة في الكفر , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r6.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who scattered decayed bones and challenged the possibility of resurrection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p179/r6.anchor: وذكر الكلبي أن هذه الآية نزلت في أبي بن خلف الجمحي حين أخذ عظاما نخرة فذراها

MUQATIL:16:3-5/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:3-5/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:3-5/r2.claim: The human created from a sperm drop is Ubayy b. Khalaf al-Jumahi, whom the Prophet killed at Uhud.

MUQATIL:16:3-5/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:3-5/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:3-5/r3.claim: Ubayy challenged the Prophet about how God could resurrect bones, crushing and scattering them in the wind; the same challenge appears in 36:78.
MUQATIL:16:3-5/r3.anchor: وجعل يفتها ويذريها في الريح، نظيرها في آخر يس

NASAFI-FULL:v2p249#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p249#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p249#4/r1.claim: The human becomes an articulate disputant after beginning as an insensible, motionless drop.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p249#4/r1.anchor: فاذا هو منطبق مجادل عن نفسه مكافح لخصومه مبين لحجته بعد ما كان نطفة لاحس به ولا حركة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p249#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p249#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p249#4/r2.claim: Alternatively, he disputes with God, denying his Creator and asking who can revive decayed bones, showing insolence and ingratitude.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p249#4/r2.anchor: فاذا هو خصيم لربه منكر على خالقه قائل من يحيى العظام وهي رميم وهو وصف للانسان بالوقاحة والتمادى في كفران النعمة

QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r1.claim: After presenting proof of God's oneness, the passage turns to human resistance and excess.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r1.anchor: لما ذكر الدليل على توحيده ذكر بعده الإنسان ومناكدته وتعدي طوره

QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r2.claim: Al-insān is a generic noun referring to humankind.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r3.claim: A report identifies the person as Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who brought the Prophet a decayed bone and challenged whether God could revive it; the incident is also connected to 36:77.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r3.anchor: وروي أن المراد به أبي بن خلف الجمحي، جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم رميم

QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r4.claim: Humankind is created from fluid, developed through stages, born and grown, then becomes disputatious; the author links this explanation with 36:77.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r4.anchor: أي خلق الإنسان من ماء يخرج من بين الصلب والترائب، فنقله أطوارا

QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r5.claim: The wording expresses wonder at a human who disputes God's power, despite forgetting his own origin, as 36:78 says.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r6.claim: Khaṣīm means an argumentative disputant, like nasīb meaning munāsib; here the person disputes God's power.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r6.anchor: أي مخاصم، كالنسيب بمعنى المناسب. أي يخاصم الله عز وجل في قدرته

QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r7.claim: Mubīn may mean manifest in disputation, making a false case clear about himself, or articulating what lies within him by speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:4/r7.anchor: والمبين: هو المفصح عما في ضميره بمنطقه

BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r1.claim: الإنسان means Adam's descendants, not their first parents: Adam was created from soil and Eve from Adam's left rib.
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r1.anchor: {خلق الانسان} أي : بني آدم لا غير لأن أبويهم لم يخلقا من النطفة بل خلق آدم من التراب

BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r2.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r2.claim: Al-Qamus defines نطفة as a man's semen.

BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r3.claim: Humans begin as insentient, motionless semen without understanding or fixed form, then receive intellect and understanding.
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r3.anchor: از آب منى كه جماديست بي حس وحركت وفهم وهيولائي كه وضع وشكل نذيرد س اورافهم وعقل داد

BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r4.claim: The ف signals how quickly people forget their beginning after creation.
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r4.anchor: وأتى بالفاء إشارة إلى سرعة نسيانهم ابتداء خلقهم

BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r5.claim: خصيم describes intense argument, and مبين means either able to present clear proofs or plainly evident in his contentiousness.
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r5.anchor: {خصيم} بليغ الخصومة شديد الجدل {مبين} أي : مظهر للحجة أو ظاهر لا شبهة في زيادة خصومته وجدله

BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r6.speaker: المهدوي
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawi reports that the verse refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who brought the Prophet a decayed bone and challenged the resurrection; a similar verse near the end of Ya-Sin was revealed about him.
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r6.anchor: وقد حكى المهدوي أن المراد به أبي بن خلف الجمحي فإنه أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم رميم

BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r7.claim: From lifeless semen God gives knowledge and power, yet the human becomes an adversary to the Creator, claiming independent existence and a share in being and acts.
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r7.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" أي : جعل الإنسان من نطفة ميتة لا فعل لها ولا علم بوجودها

BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r8.claim: The verse rebukes human insolence, ignorance, and ingratitude: after being created first from clay and then semen, people grow only more arrogant.
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r8.anchor: والآية وصف الإنسان بالإفراط في الوقاحة والجهل والتمادي في كفران النعمة

BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r9.claim: The author cites the common scholarly view that semen is impure and quotes a Persian couplet to challenge human pride in such an origin.
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r9.anchor: وهم ما ازدادوا إلا تكبرا ومالهم والكبر بعد أن خلقوا من نطفة نجسة في قول عامة العلماء

BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r10.speaker: إنسان العيون
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r10.claim: Insan al-ʿUyun says the Prophet's bodily discharges are pure, a special quality; semen's ruling is less severe because it is lighter than those discharges.
BURSEVI:v5p4#2/r10.anchor: وفي "إنسان العيون" : أن فضلاته صلى الله عليه وسلم طاهرة انتهى.

RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r1.claim: After using the celestial bodies as evidence for a wise creator, Rāzī turns to the human, the noblest body after the heavens: its creation from sperm points through the body, and its disputatious intellect through the soul.
RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r1.anchor: أشرف الأجسام بعد الأفلاك والكواكب هو الإنسان ، فلما ذكر الله تعالى الاستدلال على وجود الإله الحكيم بأجرام الأفلاك

RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r2.speaker: الأطباء
RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r2.claim: Some physicians say sperm is internally heterogeneous: food undergoes four digestions in the stomach, liver, veins, and organs, whose substances form tissues; bodily heat during desire then liquefies material from the organs into sperm.
RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r2.anchor: إلا أن من الأطباء من يقول إنه مختلف الأجزاء في الحقيقة ، وذلك لأنه إنما يتولد من فضلة الهضم الرابع ، فإن الغذاء يحصل له في المعدة

RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r3.claim: If sperm is homogeneous, its inherent natural force acting by necessity on homogeneous matter should produce a sphere; since animal bodies are not spherical, their formation requires a wise, deliberate creator.
RAZI-FULL:v19p178#3/r3.anchor: فإن كان الحق هو الأول لم يجز أن يكون المقتضى لتولد البدن منها هو الطبيعة الحاصلة في جوهر النطفة

RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r1.claim: If sperm is heterogeneous, its rapidly changing parts cannot maintain their positions: brain material could settle below and heart material above, yet organs reliably form in their proper arrangement, proving wise deliberate governance.
RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r1.anchor: أن النطفة رطوبة سريعة الاستحالة ، وإذا كان كذلك كانت الأجزاء الموجودة فيها لا تحفظ الوضع والنسبة

RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r2.claim: Natural forces would make each simple constituent spherical, yielding an animal of joined spheres; celestial influences are also inadequate because they are uniform, so the bodies are governed by a wise, voluntary agent.
RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r2.anchor: من تلك البسائط يجب أن يكون شكله هو الكرة فكان يلزم أن يكون الحيوان على شكل كرات مضمومة بعضها إلى بعض

RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r3.claim: A newborn human is less perceptive than a chick, which already distinguishes danger, allies, and suitable food; later the human mind reaches extraordinary knowledge and disputation, a transition from deficiency to perfection requiring wise divine governance.
RAZI-FULL:v19p179/r3.anchor: ولد الدجاجة كما يخرج من قشر البيضة يميز بين العدو والصديق فيهرب من الهرة ويلتجىء إلى الأم

RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r1.claim: The verse abbreviates the many transformations involved in human creation because other verses already detail them, including the stages from clay extract to sperm in a secure lodging.
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r1.anchor: أنه تعالى إنما يخلق الإنسان من النطفة بواسطة تغيرات كثيرة مذكورة في القرآن العزيز

RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r2.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī glosses khaṣīm as a disputant; the lexicographers treat faʿīl as equivalent to mufāʿil, as in near relation or companion terms.
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي : الخصيم بمعنى المخاصم ، قال أهل اللغة : خصيمك الذي يخاصمك وفعيل بمعنى مفاعل

RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r3.claim: Another possible analysis makes khaṣīm an active form from khaṣama/yakhṣimu, meaning to dispute mutually; Rāzī cites Ḥamza’s reading at 36:49 as an example of the verb.
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون خصيم فاعلا من خصم يخصم بمعنى اختصم ، ومنه قراءة حمزة : { تأخذهم وهم يخصمون }

RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r4.claim: The preferred sense is that the former sperm becomes an articulate advocate, disputing with others; this transition supports the proof of a wise creator developed in the passage.
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r4.anchor: فإذا هو منطبق مجادل عن نفسه ، منازع للخصوم بعد أن كان نطفة قذرة

RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r5.claim: A second sense is that the human disputes his Lord and denies resurrection, asking who will revive decayed bones; it depicts insolence and ingratitude, but Rāzī says this fits the passage’s proof of the creator less well.
RAZI-FULL:v19p180/r5.anchor: والثاني : فإذا هو خصيم لربه ، منكر على خالقه ، قائل : { من يحي العظام وهى رميم }
